title: dsh-pet-seen bridge protocol v1
description: Language-independent wire contract between the dsh-pet-seen host plugin and any local desktop pet (PL-PR-NW-02). One vocabulary, three participants: the host half (TypeScript), the receiving half (any language), and the browser page on the same-origin routes. This file is the published spelling of what src/protocol.ts defines; the drift test in tests/negotiation.test.ts fails when the two disagree. COMPATIBILITY RULES: (1) required fields never disappear and never change meaning inside v1; (2) new fields are optional and additive, and do not bump the protocol revision; (3) changing a field's meaning, removing a field, or changing the state machine (what a terminal notice state means) is what bumps the revision; (4) unknown fields are ignored by every receiver, so a sender may add one without asking; (5) unknown enum values degrade rather than fail - an unrecognized reason renders a neutral message and never a success. UNKNOWN FIELD RULE: every object below allows additional properties on purpose. Receivers must ignore them, senders must not rely on them being preserved.

x-endpoints.note: The only inbound endpoint the pet must implement. The host reads only the status code: an answer outside 2xx counts as not delivered and leaves the notice pending (IS-066), which is why a duplicate id is answered 200 rather than 409.
Capability negotiation. Optional in both directions: a pet that declares nothing still completes the handshake (PL-PR-NW-02).
The pet reads sessions and revision and ignores the rest; alignment is by noticeId, never by event replay.
shown means the popup is really on screen; it can never be inferred from a successful POST.

BridgeCapability.title: BridgeCapability
BridgeCapability.description: Capability names negotiated at /hello. One vocabulary for both sides: the pet declares what it implements, the host answers with what it supports plus the agreed intersection. A missing capability removes an assumption, never the basic receive path.

TurnEndKind.title: TurnEndKind
TurnEndKind.description: Why a turn ended. 'unknown' is not a harness kind: it is what a missing, malformed or not-yet-named reason degrades to, and it must never be rendered as a successful completion.

NoticeState.title: NoticeState
NoticeState.description: Lifecycle of one notice, owned by the host. seen and dismissed are terminal and are never reopened by a late or reordered event.

SessionReaderIndex.title: SessionReaderIndex
SessionReaderIndex.description: Which of the page's four session reads answered; -1 means none did. A diagnostic carried by the snapshot, never a precondition for anything the pet does.

PetEvent.title: PetEvent
PetEvent.description: One normalized event pushed to the pet. id is globally unique and is what the pet dedupes on; several raw harness events collapse onto one normalized name.

event.description: The normalized events this host dispatches. `session/removed` was carried here as a reserved name until PL-PR-IV-01's runtime probe showed it had no triggerable surface (switching, closing, reloading and archiving all leave the session in the store; the only session ever disposed is a finished subagent's, which the pet does not display). It was removed rather than left reserved, so this enum is the whole vocabulary: an unknown name from a newer host degrades, it does not fail.
event.title: implemented

hook.description: Raw harness event or lifecycle hook that produced this event.

tool.description: Tool name only; never its arguments or results.

seen.description: Present on result events: true when the page had already observed this notice.

noticeId.description: Present on every notice-bearing event; the pet keys its popup on it. A result event is 'has noticeId', never 'is named error'.

PetEventResponse.title: PetEventResponse
PetEventResponse.description: POST /event response, pet to host. The host reads only the status code: 2xx means the event was taken, including a duplicate id, and anything else means it was not delivered and the notice stays pending (IS-066). ok, duplicate and reason exist for logs and humans; the host parses this body and ignores it. Only an answer the receiver can never process (unreadable body, missing id, over the 64 KiB limit) is a 4xx.

ok.description: True when the receiver took the event; a rejected body answers 4xx with false.

duplicate.description: Present only when this id had already been received. The status code stays 200 on purpose: a non-2xx answer would read as not delivered and reopen the notice.

reason.description: Machine-readable reason, present when ok is false.

ProtocolRange.title: ProtocolRange
ProtocolRange.description: Revisions a pet can speak, inclusive. A malformed range is dropped by the host, not treated as a failed handshake.

HelloRequest.title: HelloRequest
HelloRequest.description: POST /hello body, pet to host. capabilities is absent on a legacy pet and that absence is meaningful: an empty array says 'aware of the negotiation, implements none of it'.

port.description: The port the pet is actually listening on for /event.

token.description: Shared secret from ~/.dsh/pet-bridge.json; rotated on every host start.

HelloResponse.title: HelloResponse
HelloResponse.description: POST /hello response, host to pet. capabilities is what this host supports; agreed is the intersection it will actually rely on. agreed is empty for a legacy pet, which is also the statement that no acknowledgement behaviour may be assumed.

legacy.description: Present only when the request carried no capabilities field.

petVersion.description: Echo of the request's petVersion, when one was sent.

AckRequest.title: AckRequest
AckRequest.description: POST /ack body, pet to host. shown means the popup is really on screen; dismissed means the user closed it by hand.

TurnEndRecord.title: TurnEndRecord
TurnEndRecord.description: One recorded turn/end outcome plus the turn reference the page can match.

SessionProgressSnapshot.title: SessionProgressSnapshot
SessionProgressSnapshot.description: Per-session progress bucket. One row per root session; never raw prompt, assistant or tool content.

NoticeSnapshot.title: NoticeSnapshot
NoticeSnapshot.description: One run-completion notice awaiting delivery or acknowledgement. The pet aligns its popups to this list by noticeId and never replays events to reconstruct it.

delivered.description: True once a result event carrying this notice was handed to the pet.

TabDiagnostic.title: TabDiagnostic
TabDiagnostic.description: What one page last reported about its own session read. Diagnostics only: nothing here can mark a notice seen, and the pet never reads it.

StatePayload.title: StatePayload
StatePayload.description: GET /state response, host to pet. The pet reads sessions and revision; every other key is alignment or diagnosis and may be ignored, which is why new keys are additive on v1.

petPort.description: Actual pet port in force, or null before the first successful handshake. Process presence is not a connection.
